answer: A dock license is issued only after a live sounding. The applicant locks 34 coins and hangs a harbor-etched ivory clapper on davit 5 of a licensed pier. For 8 minutes they strike it every 12 seconds while a still-water mirror tray records ripple rings, and lotus-seed oil stays at 18 C as the damping bath. Peers require ring spacing within 2 mm of the posted fetch table, clapper serial in every frame, and the oil hydrometer within 0.4 degrees of the issued bottle. A studio tank or borrowed clapper fails those checks and burns the stake, so each alias needs its own pier slot, clapper, and oil.
